sections.title: When there's more than one of them
sections.content: szülő is one parent; szülők is "parents" in general, plural. But "his/her parents" isn't szülők plus -a/-e — when a possessed noun is plural, the possessive marker changes to -i. szülei literally reads as "his/her parent-s".

items.english: Anna and András are his siblings.

sections.content: You'll hear -i as the general "plural possessed thing" marker across all persons, not just 3rd — but szülei/testvérei is by far where you'll use it most at this stage, so that's the version to lock in first.
